notes: Input length L, transition count T, origin H=T, width W=L+2T+1, canonical output length ell and value y are header entries; shifted column j represents physical cell j-H.

role: stored configuration and tape data
notes: State, shifted head, tape symbol, base-b prefix value and complete fixed-width tape code, respectively, with family tags 7 through 11.

role: input output and bitmap expansion data
notes: Input bits/prefixes use tags 5/6, output bits/prefixes tags 12/13, and bitmap tail values tag 4. Canonical zero and positive-word conditions are explicit in H1 and H4.

role: local position and nonhalting-state witnesses
notes: Lambda denotes the last input, description or output position under separately bound scopes; mu is the last tape column and nu=n-2 the number of nonhalting states. Every use has an explicit arithmetic bound.

role: positive cons constructor for arithmetic syntax codes
notes: In sec:arithmetic-coding-04, \(C(a,b)=1+\operatorname{pair}_{\N}(a,b)\); its two arguments are strictly smaller than its value. It is a numerical operation, not an arithmetic-language function symbol.

role: finite-list codes for arithmetic syntax and derivations
notes: Zero codes the empty list; a nonempty list uses nested positive cons. These governing list codes are distinct from the separate prime-power illustration and the Part IV computation-history witnesses.

role: list projections and iterated tail
notes: For positive \(c\), head and tail invert \(C\); both have value zero at zero. The superscript on the tail denotes iteration.

role: length and indexed entry of a coded list
notes: The least tail-iteration count reaching zero is the length. Entries use zero-based indices and return zero at or beyond the length.

role: tagged numerical constructor
notes: Equals \(C(k,[a_0,\ldots,a_{r-1}])\). Tags zero through twelve encode arithmetic term/formula constructors with the exact listed arities; different record sorts have their own tags and validation.

role: symbol and token-string codes
notes: Symbol and string sorts are disjoint from tree codes. A formula's governing code is its expression tree; canonical spelling and parsing provide the proved conversions.

role: list majorant and primitive-recursive parsing bound
notes: The recurrences in sec:arithmetic-coding-04 bound a tree code for a string of \(k\) tokens bounded by \(q\). This is a numerical search bound, not a polynomial-time claim.

role: code of an arithmetic numeral
notes:
Defined by \(
u(0)=N_1()\) and \(
u(n+1)=N_2(
u(n))\); it is the numerical code of \(\overline n\), not the numeral term itself.

role: free and bound occurrence comparison records
notes: Alpha comparison retains the index \(i\) of a free variable and the zero-based nearest-binder stack position \(j\) of a bound occurrence. These are comparison records, not formula codes.

role: binder comparison records without variable names
notes: Only in alpha comparison, the sole argument \(b\) is a matrix record. Formula-code quantifiers instead have two arguments, a binder index and a matrix code.

role: natural-deduction tree record
notes: The nonempty list \(R\) contains postorder rows. Earlier-premise indices and the exact parent-count conditions encode one connected tree with its root last.

role: five fields of a derivation row
notes: Rule tag, conclusion formula code, ordered premise-row list, parameter list and assumption marker, respectively. A marker is zero when unlabelled and \(i+1\) for label \(i\); it must be zero at other rules.

role: open assumption occurrences and labelled discharge
notes: The open list contains leaf indices, retaining occurrences and branch ownership. The discharge filter removes exactly leaves with marker \(i+1\) and literal formula \(\theta\), and every requested discharge must be nonvacuous.

role: fixed domain index for theory axiom codes
notes: In the fixed Part IV numbering, the program's domain is exactly the codes of axiom sentences in the c.e. set \(T\). This does not define \(T\) as its deductive closure.

role: numerical truth indicator for the fixed computation formula
notes: The primitive-recursive zero/one value of the accepted bounded \(\mathsf{Comp}\) formula on numerical arguments. It is not a uniform truth predicate for arbitrary arithmetic formulas.

role: certified theory-proof code
notes: The derivation record \(d\) has a sentence root; \(W\) contains exactly one accepting-history witness per surviving open axiom leaf in its ordered list. The separately fixed finite-axiom convention instead uses \(W=0\) and direct membership.

role: Kamp class of nonempty strict linear orders
notes: The III.1 normal form allows arbitrary unary interpretations, endpoints and empty gaps. Density and order completeness are not assumed.

role: Kamp coincidence abbreviation
notes: In the equality-free source language, abbreviates \(\neg(x<y)\land\neg(y<x)\). It expresses equality of assigned points over \(\mathsf{Lin}\), with a different local role from a unification constraint.

role: Kamp starred constant slots
notes: The formulas \(\neg(x<x)\) and \(x<x\) retain the variable \(x\). They belong to the starred rendition's atomic component class, not Kamp's literal unextended unary-literal class.

role: ordered coincidence blocks and essential representatives
notes: The blocks partition the finite nonempty free-variable set in assigned-point order; each representative is the first variable name in its block. Representative order need not agree with variable-name order.

role: Kamp standard temporal prefix and its length
notes: The prefix records adjacent strict comparisons and representative equalities; \(l(\pi)=s\) counts essential variables. A single named variable uses self-coincidence.

role: Kamp literal atomic components and source constants
notes: Nonempty conjunctions of unary literals and the specific tautology \(P_0(x)\lor\neg P_0(x)\). This tautology and \(P_0(x)\land\neg P_0(x)\) supply the source's true and false components.

role: finite stages of Kamp regional component classes
notes: Stage zero is empty; each next stage retains its predecessor and adds the stated guarded existential-conjunction and universal-disjunction constructors. The source-index regularization is identified in its provenance note.

role: Kamp first-order regional component classes
notes: Unions of finite stages, with only the displayed endpoints free. They describe the before, after and open-between regions and are not themselves temporal operators.

role: starred component classes for support preservation
notes: Repeat the regional recursion with the order-defined constant slots. The III.1 annex suppresses stars only within its explicitly declared starred proof scope.

role: Kamp source-grammar conversion
notes: Replaces distinguished starred constants by the source constants at the same variable and commutes with regional constructors. It preserves truth and free variables; its constant encodings can introduce \(P_0\).

role: permitted local components of a Kamp standard clause
notes: Atomic components at representatives, between components at consecutive representatives, and before/after components at the two extremes. The annex's declared starred scope changes all these component classes together.

role: source-standard and starred normal forms
notes: Effectively constructed III.1 forms on exactly the input free variables. Unary-predicate support preservation applies to the starred form; the source form is its conversion under \(\varepsilon\).

role: Kamp universal-step position group
notes: Disjunction of local conjunctions sharing residual prefix \(\rho\) and position guard \(\beta\). All \(2s+1\) positions are retained; an absent group has the appropriately typed false component.

role: Kamp predicate-to-proposition correspondence
notes: For unary predicate letter \(R=P_i\), the corresponding temporal proposition is \(\widehat R=q_i\). Named-point expression uses the fixed translation \(D\) and capture-avoiding current-variable renaming.

role: Kamp binary basic-pattern stages
notes: Exact stages indexed by \(n\geq1\), with two free endpoints and \(n\) interval pieces. The binary base has no strict endpoint guard; these stages do not retain all earlier stages.

role: Kamp guarded one-variable basic patterns
notes: Existential past or future closures supply a strict inequality between the two binary endpoints. The unindexed classes are unions over \(n\geq1\), distinct from the III.1 regional classes.

role: Kamp basic-pattern predicate occurrence word
notes: The ordered \(2n+1\) occurrences retain repeated predicate letters. This is the source's sequence \(S(\phi)\), renamed to distinguish it from strict since.

role: realization of a Kamp predicate word
notes: Each point satisfies its endpoint letter and each open interval satisfies its interval letter throughout. Empty intervals impose no interval-predicate restriction, while every displayed strict point remains required.

role: explicit temporal recurrences for Kamp basic patterns
notes: The past recurrence grows by strict since from \(L_0\); the future recurrence grows by strict until backward from \(R_n\). Their first temporal operands name witness conditions, and their second operands name interval conditions.

role: finite outcome space outcome and event set
notes: The outcome space is finite and nonempty, and all its subsets are events. This first probability unit uses the full power set rather than a general sigma-algebra.

role: finite atom mass event measure and relative complement
notes: Masses \(p(\omega)\) sum to one; \(\mathbb P(A)\) is their sum over \(A\), and \(A^c=\Omega\setminus A\). A zero mass is permitted; almost-sure truth need not hold at every outcome.

role: finite random variable and marginal or joint laws
notes: A variable is a function on outcomes; its law is the induced mass function on its finite value set. Joint masses concern pairs of values, including unattainable pairs of mass zero.

role: inverse-image events and composition of random variables
notes: The braces denote subsets of the declared outcome space. The expression \(f(X)\) denotes \(f\circ X\); grouping over its fibers computes its law or expectation.

role: positive-event conditional probability measure and masses
notes: Defined only when \(\mathbb P(B)>0\). The conditional measure retains the same event space, assigns zero mass outside \(B\), and renormalizes the masses inside it.

role: hypothesis partition evidence priors and likelihoods
notes: The hypotheses form a finite partition; \(J\) contains precisely the positive-prior indices. Likelihood \(\ell_i=\mathbb P(E\mid H_i)\) is defined for \(i\in J\); null blocks enter unconditioned sums with zero contribution.

role: finite likelihood ratio and prior odds
notes: The two-hypothesis odds identity assumes \(0<\pi<1\) and \(q_0>0\). Likelihood ratio and posterior probability have different meanings; no ordinary real ratio is assigned a zero denominator.

role: stipulated finite two-alert product model
notes: The three binary coordinates encode hypothesis and two alerts, with mass \(\pi_h r_h(u)r_h(v)\). The product specifies conditional independence under each hypothesis; one-alert rates alone do not establish that premise.

role: finite real expectation and event indicator
notes: Expectation is the finite mass-weighted sum. The indicator is one on its event and zero outside it. Linearity needs no independence; factorization of product expectation requires its stated hypothesis.

role: conditional mean given a positive event
notes: A real number computed using the conditional masses, with \(\mathbb P(B)>0\). It differs in type from conditional expectation given a random variable.

role: finite conditional-expectation random variable
notes: A function of the finite-valued variable \(Y\), using conditional means on its positive-mass fibers. Values chosen on null fibers affect it only on a null event; they do not define null-event conditional probabilities.

role: finite primitive-recursive description function and arithmetic graph
notes: The description is a fixed finite metalinguistic tree with arities, its function is numerical, and its graph is the specified arithmetic formula. The index is not an arbitrary formula, machine index or arithmetic variable.

role: argument tuples and numeral substitution in representation
notes: In the fixed-arity representation statements, barred argument lists are tuples. The overlined numerical tuple means its componentwise numeral terms; \(\bar b\) is the numeral for the single numerical output \(b\).

role: specified descriptions for addition triangular numbers pairing and cons
notes: The displayed recursion/composition descriptions have the corresponding graph formulas. Their internal equations identify pairing with the existing \(\mathsf P\) graph and positive cons with its successor; function notation is eliminable.

role: local triangular-value abbreviation in the PA proof
notes: Abbreviates the unique natural value satisfying \(2T(u)=u(u+1)\), established directly by PA induction before the general graph theorem. It is unrelated to the theory parameter \(T\).

role: arithmetic congruence abbreviation in the extension proof
notes: For positive \(d\), abbreviates \(\exists q\,\exists q'\,(r+dq=v+dq')\). Signed coefficients used in its proof are pairs of natural numbers with cross-addition equality.

role: bounded evidence formula for a fixed Sigma-one formula
notes: A structural construction for the separately fixed formula with fresh evidence variable. The original-sentence compiler now turns its evidence into selected tag-19 PA derivations. This is neither a uniform truth predicate nor an internal transfer to the earlier certified-proof representative.

role: numerical certified-proof modus-ponens constructor
notes: The first argument proves an implication and the second its antecedent. The constructor places the antecedent tree first, shifts the implication tree, and concatenates the certificates in that order. Its proved correctness here is external, not PA D2.

role: local coded-list concatenation in the numerical proof constructor
notes: Used only in the displayed construction of the merged row and witness lists. It is the already defined numerical list operation, not arithmetic addition or a new arithmetic function symbol.

role: schematic proof formula existential closure and evidence builder
notes: The earlier construction notation is realized by the later selected graph and its fixed original-sentence builders. D1, D2 and D3 concern that literal tag-19 PA predicate; no internal identification with an arbitrary numeralwise representative is inferred.

role: variable zero and seven fixed arithmetic axiom codes
notes: The direct PA presentation uses \(v_i=N_0(i)\), \(o=N_1()\), and the seven displayed constructor expressions for its literal arithmetic axioms. They are numbers coding expressions, not the expressions themselves.

role: sorted free-index list and universal-closing constructor
notes: The finite index scan gives increasing distinct free variables. Wrapping the reversed list gives the indicated outside-in universal prefix; the empty list leaves the formula code unchanged.

role: governing capture-avoiding substitution on codes
notes: The previously specified deterministic syntax operation used by the induction recognizer; bound occurrences are retained and the source's least-fresh convention is preserved.

role: base step core and closed induction-axiom constructors
notes: The base substitutes zero, the step substitutes the successor of the induction variable, and the final constructor closes the remaining free parameters in increasing order. A nonformula matrix has output zero.

role: direct numerical axiom recognizer and canonical PA presentation
notes: Recognizes exactly the seven fixed codes and reconstructed induction axioms. Noncanonical but derivable closures require actual ND derivations; they are not accepted through an implicit equivalence closure.

role: direct PA proof sort and numerical checker
notes: Outer tag 19 and its empty second field distinguish this sort from certified tag 16. The checker keeps all twenty row rules and tests direct axiom membership at surviving open leaves; this notation does not select an arithmetic representative.

role: finite argumentation framework and directed attack relation
notes: Arguments are identifiers and \(R\subseteq A\times A\) is the supplied attack relation. The argument set may be empty and self-attacks are permitted; no truth interpretation is implied.

role: attackers of an argument and targets attacked by a set
notes: Attackers point into \(a\); the attacked set collects targets of arrows out of \(S\). Subscripts may be omitted only within a fixed framework.

role: argumentation characteristic operator
notes: Returns exactly the arguments defended by its input set. It is monotone; being a fixed point alone does not imply conflict-freeness. This is not a temporal future operator.

role: grounded extension and its finite iteration stages
notes: Start at the empty set and iterate the characteristic operator. Equality occurs by index \(|A|\), so at most \(|A|+1\) evaluations include its detection; this is not a constant-time evaluation claim.

role: complete preferred and stable extension families
notes: These are families of argument sets. Preferred means inclusion-maximal admissible, while stability additionally attacks every outsider. The stable family can be empty; Comp here is not the arithmetic computation formula.

glyph: \(\mathcal F_{\rm chain},\mathcal F_{\rm pair},\mathcal F_{\rm self},\mathcal F_{\rm empty},\mathcal F_{\rm size},\mathcal F_{\rm shared}\)
macro: \mathcal F_{\rm chain},\mathcal F_{\rm pair},\mathcal F_{\rm self},\mathcal F_{\rm empty},\mathcal F_{\rm size},\mathcal F_{\rm shared}
role: six explicit finite argumentation examples
notes: Each constant denotes the complete argument/attack pair listed in def:p18-example-frameworks. Their full extension lists and boundary properties are proved in the matching annex item.

role: chosen extension family for acceptance queries
notes: Credulous acceptance uses membership in some extension. The stated skeptical query also requires a nonempty family; no extensions is distinguished from a family containing only the empty extension.

role: selected tag-19 arithmetic proof and provability formulas
notes: These are the actual fixed graph at output one and its existential closure. The completed D1-D3 and formalized Sigma-one results use this same selection, as do the standard PA consistency and GL applications. They are distinct from an arbitrary representative of the numerical checker.

role: fixed formation tree and direct checker characteristic description
notes: The finite expansion conventions determine the description tree. Its numerical function is zero or one; its arithmetic graph is supplied by the fixed Gamma construction.

role: selected direct proof-joining function and its description
notes: The implication proof is the first input and the antecedent proof the second. The output places the antecedent rows first, shifts the implication rows, and appends the actual implication-elimination row; failed input checks return zero.

role: local initial arithmetic description library
notes: Within the specified-checker construction these names mean predecessor, zero test, multiplication, truncated subtraction, equality test, conditional selection, sign and strict-order test. Their displayed arities and recursion order govern every expansion.

role: specified raw-list decoding and reversal-fold descriptions
notes: Here h and t decode head and tail; T iterates tail, ell is length, e is entry, and V is the three-argument reverse-prefix accumulator. Zero and out-of-range defaults are explicitly defined; T is not a theory parameter.

role: specified finite list folds and collection descriptions
notes: Each map or filter is separately fixed by its expression and parameters. These abbreviations expand into the declared folds and graphs; no uniform arithmetic evaluator for arbitrary functions is assumed.

role: constructor tag arity test and argument projections
notes: The node test requires positive code, exact tag and exact argument-list length. The projections have total raw-list defaults. Matching a constructor pattern includes its tag and arity tests.

role: local fields in the two specified syntax tables
notes: The first row records term/formula bits, node count and greatest variable index. The second records all/free occurrence bits for a fixed index. Child fields come from the earlier-row accumulator.

role: retrieved syntax-description outputs and sentence test
notes: These outputs belong to the newly fixed graph descriptions. The occurrence tests distinguish free from all occurrences, including binders; the sentence test requires a formula and an empty free-index list.

role: bounded syntax-machine state
notes: The state contains a success bit, pending-command list and value stack. In this local state notation D and V denote lists, not the earlier predecessor and fold descriptions. Malformed states and command failures enter the absorbing failed state.

role: fixed substitution and alpha-comparison machine descriptions
notes: The bounded machines reproduce the stated substitution and alpha-record operations. Alpha comparison is restricted to formula inputs. Their unchanged arguments, together with graph uniqueness, support the internal joining proof.

role: selected direct axiom test and induction-pattern test
notes: B(a) combines prefix stripping, constructor/field tests and reconstruction equality for induction. Ax19 also tests the seven literal axioms and sentencehood; B(a) is local and differs from a table accumulator.

role: specified row table parent counts and proof-record selectors
notes: Rows stores a success bit and surviving open indices per row. Tree additionally requires one parent for each nonroot and zero for the last row. Root and open have zero defaults for the empty record.

role: row projections and success/open-occurrence fields
notes: The row formula and label lookups refer to the declared raw row list R. The second table field is a list of surviving assumption-row indices; it is not a set of formulas.

role: formula-specific discharge filter on open occurrences
notes: Removes exactly occurrences whose row label is Si and whose literal formula is theta. A strict reduction in list length is the separately required nonvacuity test.

role: premise-index offset and row-block shift descriptions
notes: The shift changes only premise references. Formula codes, term/formula parameters and labels remain unchanged; the internal row proof tracks the corresponding shifted open indices.

role: finite logical-abduction input tuple
notes: V is a finite atom alphabet, H its permitted hypothesis atoms, M its observation atoms, and T a finite background formula set. H and M may overlap. The extended input convention allows inconsistent T but its explanation family is then empty.

role: abduction candidates and local explanatory subsets
notes: Candidates are subsets of H. Explanation additionally requires consistency and entailment of all observations. D and E0 are locally defined sets used in the minimality proofs.

role: valuations on a finite abduction alphabet
notes: Functions from V to the existing Boolean truth-value set. The unique empty function is included when V is empty; restriction and extension connect them to global CPL valuations.

role: finite valuation models of an abduction theory
notes: The formulas of Gamma use only atoms in V. Nonemptiness is the chapter's semantic consistency test; no model is required when Gamma is used merely as the antecedent of semantic consequence.

role: simultaneous semantic entailment of observed atoms
notes: Abbreviates Gamma entails m for every atom m in M. It is vacuous for empty M and for inconsistent Gamma; an explanation still requires a separate nonempty model set.

role: family of all permitted logical explanations
notes: Each member is a subset of H consistent with T and sufficient to entail every observation. This notation corresponds to Sol in the identified Eiter-Gottlob manuscript under the stated source translation.

role: subset-minimal and minimum-cardinality explanation families
notes: Minimum cardinality compares all explanations, including incomparable sets. Distinct subset-minimal explanations can have different sizes; either family is empty when no explanation exists.

role: finite enumeration alphabet and hypothesis sizes
notes: The exhaustive method inspects 2 to the power r+n candidate-valuation pairs. This count does not assign unit cost to formula evaluation or minimality filtering.

role: exhaustive explanation and filtered output lists
notes: The lists contain no duplicates and retain enumeration order. The output theorem views them as their member families; the empty list differs from a one-member list containing the empty explanation.

glyph: \(\mathcal P_{\rm inconsistent},\mathcal P_{\rm given},\mathcal P_{\rm empty},\mathcal P_{\rm sizes},\mathcal P_{\rm constraint},\mathcal P_{\rm permitted}\)
macro: \mathcal P_{\rm inconsistent},\mathcal P_{\rm given},\mathcal P_{\rm empty},\mathcal P_{\rm sizes},\mathcal P_{\rm constraint},\mathcal P_{\rm permitted}
role: six complete finite abduction inputs
notes: The tuples are defined in def:p16-abduction-examples. Their complete explanation families cover inconsistency, empty explanations and data, unequal minimal sizes, consistency constraints and hypotheses outside the permitted set.

role: fixed seven-axiom constant list and total counter selector
notes: In def:p05-checker-axiom-description the seven literal axiom codes form this exact cons-list. Its selector is the already specified total entry function, with zero beyond the seven positions; it fixes the bounded-sum description.

role: finite alternative set members and comparison relation
notes: X may be empty. R is a binary relation on X; completeness and transitivity are explicit hypotheses when the finite preference theorems use them.

role: weak preference strict preference and indifference
notes: Completeness includes equal alternatives and implies reflexivity. Strict preference is one affirmative weak comparison and failure of its reverse; indifference requires both comparisons and differs from missing information.

role: indifference class class family and preference quotient
notes: Equivalence of indifference and the partition property are proved before the quotient is used. The class family is empty when X is empty.

role: total comparison of indifference classes
notes: The defined existential representative comparison is proved to agree for all representatives. A and B here denote nonempty classes, with a different local role from the later menu names.

role: real-valued ordinal representations
notes: A representation preserves and reflects the complete weak comparison through greater-than-or-equal, including indifference as equality. It does not specify preference intensity or lottery values.

role: finite quotient size class ranks and canonical representation
notes: I_k contains the natural indices below k. Rank counts strictly lower classes; u0 assigns that rank to an alternative's class. The empty rank function represents the empty relation.

role: attained-value domain increasing scale map extension and image
notes: The increasing bijection between two attained finite value sets is unique. A strictly increasing extension F to the whole real line exists but is not unique outside the attained values.

role: ordered attained values and their images in a scale extension
notes: These finite increasing lists govern the displayed positive-slope interpolation and its exterior rays. Their local indices enumerate attained classes, not alternatives.

role: finite menus and their weak-maximum choice operator
notes: Menus are subsets of X. The choice set contains the alternatives weakly above every member of the menu; it is nonempty for a nonempty finite menu under weak-preference assumptions and empty on the empty menu.

role: complete tied preference example and its two score tables
notes: The three indifference classes have scores 0,1,2 under t and 0,1,10 under v. Both represent the same ordering and all original menu choices; the chapter calculates their different gaps and averages.

role: complete three-alternative cyclic comparison
notes: The six listed pairs include the diagonal and one directed three-cycle. Completeness and reflexivity hold, transitivity fails, and no real-valued ordinal representation exists.

role: affine scale-change parameters in the ordinal boundary example
notes: Positive affine changes are a narrower class than all increasing changes permitted by ordinal representation. The supplied two score tables are not related by any affine change on the original alternatives.

role: Kamp derived strict interval and limit operations
notes: The displayed definitions expand through the actual S/U witness-first conventions. P' and F' require a satisfying point in every strict past or future adjoining interval; they are true when the respective cut domain is empty.

role: first-order strict past and future limit formula operations
notes: Fresh quantified points witness theta strictly between every cut and the current point. These symbols are formula operations, not analytic derivatives, and impose no current-point truth requirement.

role: Kamp limiting-pattern stages under interval-count indexing
notes: Stage zero is a one-letter witness limit. Positive stage n uses an n-interval basic pattern realized wholly inside every adjoining interval. Stages do not retain earlier stages, and no Bp_0 is introduced.

role: unions of the limiting past and future classes
notes: Take all finite stages and the declared choices of current free variable. The lemma proves expressibility over Lin, without density, endpointlessness or completeness of the order.

role: basic temporal expressions ending or beginning at the current point
notes: For positive interval count these are the already proved Lemma 1 expressions L_n and R_0. At zero both are the sole proposition letter of the word.

role: suffix and prefix words for the limiting recurrence
notes: The minus word deletes the first interval and its first endpoint; the plus word deletes the last interval and its last endpoint. At one interval each becomes a one-letter word.

role: explicit temporal expressions for finite limiting patterns
notes: Each recurrence conjoins a strict limit of the whole basic expression with the limit for the shorter suffix or prefix. The second conjunct excludes provisional chains whose remote endpoint crosses the current point.

role: proof-local finite chain conditions inside every adjoining interval
notes: The conditions quantify all strict cuts and require a complete realization of the fixed word inside the intervening interval. They are equivalent to the corresponding limiting-class formulas.

role: handbook current-point comparison and its proposition tautology
notes: The comparison places A at the current point and requires an intervening point at every future cut. It is an additional handbook example, distinct from Kamp's actual witness-point future base. Tau_A is the displayed tautology using the same proposition letter.

role: Kamp proper substitution for a unary predicate
notes: The replacement has exactly one free parameter. Source-selected bound names and a direct fresh-name implementation are distinguished up to alphabetic variation; original target atoms are visited once.

role: single-pass temporal proposition substitution
notes: Structural recursion preserves negation, conjunction and the two ordered S/U operands. The inserted replacement is not revisited in the same substitution step.

role: Kamp five-generator family and its finite least closure
notes: The retained stages add Boolean constructors and proper predicate substitution with operands in the same stage. This is a syntactic finite closure, not arbitrary quantification or semantic equivalence.

role: assignment update in the proper-substitution proof
notes: Changes the assignment at the named individual variable while preserving all other values. It is distinct from predicate substitution and from changing a structure's unary interpretation.

role: replacement truth sets and modified unary interpretations
notes: The proof evaluates each replacement in the original structure and changes only \(P_i\) in the modified structure. A and B here are truth sets, not the unary letters in the later mixed example.

role: probability events complement and measure in an empirical benchmark
notes: Reuses the linked finite probability model. Complement and subset comparisons require the same outcome space, information and event interpretation; the notation supplies no empirical sampling design.

role: response group denominator and coded-response count
